name: Gandhi
hook: The lawyer who turned nonviolence into a weapon — salt, satyagraha and the 1982 film.

facts.label: Salt March
facts.statement: Gandhi marched to the sea to make salt in defiance of the British salt tax, calling it a blow to the foundations of the Empire.

facts.label: satyagraha
facts.statement: Gandhi's philosophy of nonviolence, or satyagraha, is honored on October 2, his birthday, as an international day.

facts.label: South Africa
facts.statement: Gandhi lived in South Africa during the Boer War and served the British there as a medical volunteer.

facts.label: London law degree
facts.statement: As a teenager Gandhi left India for London, where he studied law and met Christians who shaped his religious quest.

facts.label: Harijan
facts.statement: Gandhi called the untouchables Harijan, or children of God, and campaigned against their treatment as a demeaned caste.

facts.label: Gandhi (1982 film)
facts.statement: Richard Attenborough's 1982 film Gandhi won Best Picture, with Ben Kingsley playing Gandhi.

facts.label: Martin Luther King, Jr.
facts.statement: Martin Luther King, Jr. adopted Gandhi's ideas of nonviolence while studying at Crozer Theological Seminary in the 1950s.
